title: slot-aware-dynamic-batch-growth-probe
content:
Summary:
This note captures a set of exploratory probes for a slot-aware dynamic batch-growth controller. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency under mixed workloads while preserving throughput and fairness across tenant/service tiers. This differs from previous continuous-batching experiments by explicitly tracking 'slot occupancy' (lightweight per-queue slot counters) and letting batch growth be multiplicative per-slot with a feedback term based on observed flush latency percentiles.

Background / motivation:
- We see recurring p99 spikes under medium burst traffic where naive growth (global multiplicative) causes large batches to form in a busy slot and stall smaller, low-QPS tenants.
- Existing heuristics use timeouts + max-batch to limit worst-case latency, but they do not adapt quickly to per-slot skew.
- Hypothesis: slot-aware multiplicative growth (grow smaller slots faster, cap growth when slot contributes to p99) will reduce tail without compromising median or throughput.

Concrete goals:
- Primary metric: system p99 of server-response-time (end-to-end, request received -> first token emitted). Target: reduce p99 by at least 18% vs baseline under the mixed microburst workload.
- Secondary metrics: p95, p50, throughput (tokens/sec), average batch size, fairness index (Jain's index over per-tenant latency).
- Safety: no >5% regression on p50 or throughput.

Hypotheses:
1) Per-slot growth dampens slot monopolization: if a single slot accumulates many inflight requests, multiplicative factor decreases for that slot only.
2) Using a percentile-driven feedback (p90 flush) to cap growth reduces intermittent overgrowth that leads to long kernel queues.
3) Small delta on timeouts (20% lower than default) combined with dynamic growth will improve p99 under low-latency SLO tenants.

Probe design (test matrix):
- Controller variants (A/B/C):
  A. Baseline: global multiplicative growth (current mainline).
  B. Slot-aware multiplicative growth: growth factor g_slot = g_global * (1 / (1 + log(1 + slots_occupied))) with p90 feedback cap.
  C. Slot-aware + aggression-limiter: same as B but with an aggression window that freezes growth after any slot p95 > threshold for 200ms.

- Timeouts: default (30ms), lowered (24ms), and conservative (40ms).
- Workloads: steady low-QPS, mixed microburst (50–300 qps in 200ms bursts across 20 tenants), skewed hotspot (one tenant 60% traffic), and synthetic long-context (tokens>1024) to stress KV cache interactions.

Instrumentation to add / metrics collected:
- Per-slot counters: slots_occupied, slot_pending_ms_hist (p50/p90/p99), avg_batch_size_slot.
- Global traces: batch_age_histogram (time from first request to flush), kernel_queue_depth, GPU_util_percent.
- Per-tenant: SLO-violation-rate (latency > configured SLO), tokens_served, batches_created.
- Existing traces: microtraces used by tracer-backed-batcher but extended with slot_id and slot_growth_factor at flush time.

Run plan:
- Canary small-scale (1 node runtime) with synthetic workload for functional correctness (Jan 6–8).
- Medium scale (8-node cluster, realistic mix recorded from production) for 12-hour runs to capture diurnal effects (Jan 10–12).
- Long-run soak (24h) for the most promising variant to observe rare spikes (Jan 14).

Observed results (summary table from Jan 10 medium-scale run):
- Baseline (A), mixed microburst: p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 210ms, throughput 78k tokens/s, avg_batch_size 11.
- B (slot-aware), mixed microburst: p50 19ms, p95 58ms, p99 165ms, throughput 76k tokens/s, avg_batch_size 10.2.
- C (slot-aware + limiter), mixed microburst: p50 20ms, p95 60ms, p99 152ms, throughput 75.5k tokens/s, avg_batch_size 9.8.
- Notes: variant C reduces p99 the most (28% relative to baseline) at cost of ~3% throughput. p50 stayed within 11% of baseline (safe).

Detailed observations and traces:
- Trace sample #112233 (B): slot_id=7 shows rapid growth from batch_size=3 -> 28 within 180ms; p90 flush time rose sharply and the feedback cap reduced subsequent growth for slot 7. This prevented a subsequent stall where kernel queue would have grown by 2x.
- In A, global growth allowed the hotspot tenant to accumulate very large batches; GPU kernel runtime increased nonlinearly (due to attention cost at sequence length distribution), causing long kernel latencies and backpressure cascades.
- Variant C's aggression window prevented oscillations where a slot would shrink and regrow repeatedly (observed in B). The freeze time seems important to avoid thrash.

Fairness analysis:
- Jain's fairness index for per-tenant p95 latency: A=0.72, B=0.80, C=0.84. So slot-aware approaches improved fairness (less variance between tenants).

Tradeoffs / caveats:
- Small throughput penalty (2–4%) mainly due to more conservative batch growth on heavy slots — acceptable for SLO-focused customers but maybe not for throughput-optimized backend tiers. Consider a service-tier override.
- Complexity: additional per-slot state increases memory footprint and adds a few extra atomic ops in the hot path. Measured CPU overhead: +1.1% at 8-node cluster peak.
- Edge cases: long-context synthetic workload saw slight p95 regressions in B (due to earlier inactivity-triggered growth); variant C handled it better.

Unresolved questions / experiments to follow up:
- How does slot-aware growth interact with KV cache warmup? Do we need a different growth policy while cache prefill is happening?
- Auto-tuning: can we replace fixed thresholds (p90 cap, aggression-window) with a small RL policy or bandit tuner that optimizes for p99 subject to throughput constraint?
- Interactions with routing: if smart-routing directs cold tenants off to separate slots, does slot-aware growth still provide benefit? We should replicate with smart-routing enabled.

Proposed next steps and concrete action items:
- Add feature flag gating for slot-aware controller and aggression window (PR #987, code owner Marcus).
- Run a focused experiment with customer-tier overrides: allow "throughput-tier" to bypass slot caps and measure impact (Evelyn to coordinate).
- Add a small auto-tuner PoC that searches aggression_window ∈ {100,200,400ms} and p90_cap ∈ {1.2x,1.5x,2x} using 4 warmup runs (Jon).
- Draft runbook entries: when to flip feature flag, how to roll back, monitoring alerts (SLO regression, drop in tokens/sec).

Notes to self / informal thoughts (scratch):
- The multiplicative formula above felt ad-hoc; replacing log() with a sigmoid that saturates earlier might reduce the CPU overhead of repeated log calls. Micro-optimizations: precompute a small LUT for slot sizes 0..128.
- Consider an alternate growth signal: kernel_queue_latency derivative (d/dt) rather than percentile alone — might detect imminent stalls earlier.
- We should add a synthetic test that intentionally saturates GPU with long sequences while slowly ramping QPS to study nonlinearity.

Appendix: sample trace excerpt (flattened):
- trace_id=112233, slot=7, growth_history=[(t0: size=3,g=1.4),(t0+60ms: size=8,g=2.1),(t0+180ms: size=28,g=4.0 capped->2.0)], flush_p90=172ms, kernel_queue_depth_peak=18

Quick checklist before wider rollout:
- [ ] PR review and unit tests for slot state lifecycle (creation/eviction).
- [ ] Load-test with smart-routing on/off.
- [ ] Add dashboard tiles: per-slot avg_batch_size heatmap, slot_growth_suppression_rate, p99 delta by tenant.
- [ ] Update canary alert: if p50 regresses >10% or throughput drops >7% in canary -> auto rollback.

If helpful, I can convert this into a short slides deck for the eng-rls meeting and attach the medium-scale run graphs (throughput vs time, p99 heatmap).

-- Priya
